title: Precise definition of a circle

questions.skill: Precise definition of a circle
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Write a precise definition of a circle. Base it on the notions of point, plane, and distance (you may use ordinary words such as "set", "all", and "given"). Name the center and the radius in your definition.
questions.prompt_markup: Write a precise definition of a circle. Base it on the notions of point, plane, and distance (you may use ordinary words such as "set", "all", and "given"). Name the center and the radius in your definition.
questions.correct_answer: A circle is the set of all points in a plane that are a given positive distance (the radius) from a given point in that plane (the center).
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent wording. Essential: (1) ALL points, (2) in one plane, (3) at one fixed positive distance, (4) from one fixed point, the center. Not accepted: "a round shape" (not precise); leaving out the plane (that describes a sphere); "points within a distance" (that is a disk).

questions.prompt: Kai writes: "A circle is a round curve with a center." Explain what makes this imprecise, and rewrite it as a precise definition.
questions.prompt_markup:
Kai writes: "A circle is a round curve with a center."
Explain what makes this imprecise, and rewrite it as a precise definition.
questions.correct_answer: "Round" and "curve" are not defined, and the center is not tied to the points. Precise: a circle is the set of all points in a plane at a given positive distance (the radius) from a given point in that plane (the center).
questions.grading_note: Any equivalent answer. Essential: names an undefined or vague term ("round", "curve") or the missing equal-distance condition, and gives a definition with all points, one plane, one fixed positive distance, and a center.

questions.prompt_markup:
Proposed definition: "A circle is a set of points that are all the same distance from a point O."
Give a set that fits this wording but is NOT a circle.
questions.correct_answer: For example, two points that are each 3 cm from O (or an arc of a circle, or a sphere). The definition must say ALL points at that distance, in one plane.
questions.grading_note: Any set that fits the wording but is not a whole circle: finitely many points, an arc, or a sphere.
